what: Margin rubric. What a correct answer to one lesson question needs and what each score means, written by Margin on a teacher's key. Keyed by a fingerprint of the question; no question text, no student work, no names.

rubric.asks: Who else besides enslaved people is affected by slavery, and how
rubric.note: Warmup opinion question; any reasonable ripple effect counts, including guesses about families, laws, money, or power.

bands.means: Names at least one group or part of society beyond enslaved people and says how it is affected.
Names someone or something else affected, but does not say how it is affected.
Talks only about harm to enslaved people, or gives a vague idea with no group named.
Mentions slavery but offers no idea about who else it touches.

examples.answer: It changes the laws for everybody, because the government has to make rules saying slavery is allowed and that affects whole towns.
I think it affects the economy and the laws of Texas too.
Slavery was really bad and hurt the people who were enslaved.
Slavery happened in Texas a long time ago.
